🌐 Browser Tabs & Memory

Each browser tab uses 100-300MB of memory. The more tabs you have open, the more memory your browser uses.

Chrome: Using 4.1GB across 14 processes
  • Close tabs you're not actively using
  • Use bookmarks instead of keeping tabs open
  • Consider a tab suspender extension (pauses unused tabs)
  • Each tab = 100-300MB of memory
Safari: Using 1.8GB across 6 processes
  • Close tabs you're not actively viewing
  • Use Reading List or bookmarks to save pages
  • Each tab/page = 100-200MB of memory
  • Right-click tabs → Close Other Tabs (keeps only current)
💡 Quick Tips:
  • Bookmark it: If you'll need it later, bookmark it instead of keeping the tab open
  • Close unused tabs: If you haven't looked at a tab in 10 minutes, close it
  • One window rule: Try to keep all tabs in one browser window
  • Restart browser: If memory is high, quit and reopen your browser

💡 Quick Wins:

  • Close apps you're not using right now - start with the biggest memory hogs
  • Quit browser tabs you're not actively viewing
  • Chrome: Close tabs or use tab suspender extensions
  • Restart your Mac if problems persist - clears memory cruft

📋 NEXT STEPS

  1. Check memory pressure - If 🔴 high, take action immediately
  2. Close unused apps - Right-click app in Dock → Quit
  3. Reduce browser tabs - Chrome & Safari: Close tabs or use tab suspender extensions
  4. Check Messages - Consider archiving old conversations if using lots of memory
  5. Restart if needed - Clears memory cruft and refreshes system
